description: Single source of truth for Beam performance budgets. Consumed by the CI gate (swift run perf-gate) and the in-app perf HUD. 'budget' is the design target; 'gate' is the CI failure threshold. tier 'pr' = deterministic or dev-machine-runnable; 'rig' = requires the dedicated two-machine LAN rig; 'weekly' = long-running.

conventions.latency: All timing metrics report p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max. Budgets specify which statistic they constrain. Never gate on the mean.
conventions.baselineComparison: In addition to absolute gates, any metric regressing >5% versus the baseline commit is reported; >15% fails.
conventions.e2eMethod: Clock-sync-free round-trip decomposition: E2E = RTT/2 + d_remote. See PLAN.md 3.1.
conventions.clockDomain: t0 is NSEvent.timestamp (IOHID, mach/systemUptime domain); present times are CAMetalDrawable.presentedTime / MTLCommandBuffer gpu times, same domain. Never compare timestamps across machines.
conventions.cameraOffsetNote: Constant software-presented -> photon offset, derived once per rig by 240fps camera per PLAN.md 3.1. null = not yet calibrated; photon metrics cannot be claimed until set.

L0_physical_floor.note: Calibration only, never a gate. Measured per rig so higher layers report overhead above the wire.

launch_to_first_frame_ms.note: Process exec (kinfo_proc start time) to first drawable presented. Includes runtime Metal shader compile — deliberately, so it is owned by a budget.

launch_to_typeable_ms.note: First frame presented with key window + first responder accepting keystrokes. Phase 0: same instant as first frame by construction; kept separate so it can diverge and be caught.

launch_to_peers_visible_ms.note: App launch (process exec) to a peer row PRESENTED in the roster — the launch screen IS the peer list, so this is the first thing a user sees resolve. Photon-adjacent (CAMetalDrawable.presentedTime), not a model-update timestamp. Phase 2 wires the full path against a real advertised peer.
launch_to_peers_visible_ms.method: beam --bench-join (guest, cold-launched into a network that already has a peer)

linked_dylibs.note: otool -L on the release binary. Catches accidental dependency creep.

keystroke_to_commit_p50_ms.note: NSEvent.timestamp -> command buffer committed + present() called. The pure software path; refresh-rate independent.

keystroke_to_presented_60hz_p50_ms.note: NSEvent.timestamp -> CAMetalDrawable.presentedTime, 60 Hz dev panel, MEASURED FLOOR of the naive one-shot present path (2026-08-30: phase-uniform distribution = uniform(0..16.7) + ~17 ms constant — an idle window's present misses the imminent vsync and lands a full frame later; displaySyncEnabled=false shows the non-vsync machinery is ~5 ms). Holding the line here; halving it via present-path engineering (display-link-aligned presents, presentsWithTransaction, direct-to-display — camera-decided) is Phase 1's headline objective with the aspirational numbers on the 120hz/photon rows. See PLAN.md 5-L2.

keystroke_to_photon_120hz_p50_ms.note: Camera-verified: presented_120hz + conventions.cameraOffsetMs. Cannot be reported until cameraOffsetMs is calibrated.

keystroke_to_presented_60hz_min_ms.note: PIPELINE DEPTH: the luckiest keystroke's latency — how fast the present path can possibly show a glyph. Validated 17.0 ms 2026-08-30 (a whole extra frame of pipeline); the Phase-1 present-path work is judged by driving this down, and this gate stops it creeping up meanwhile.

presented_spread_p99_minus_p50_60hz_ms.note: JITTER as a first-class metric: the tail is the UX. p99 minus p50 of keystroke->presented. Validated 7.96 ms with the hybrid render loop (was 13.0 on the naive path).

burst_125hz_presented_p99_60hz_ms.note: 150 keystrokes at 8 ms — faster than key repeat. Accounting is worst-case-honest: each coalesced frame records its OLDEST keystroke. Validated 48.6 ms with in-frame coalescing (no drops, no starvation; naive per-key presents starved the drawable queue). Scales down with pipeline depth — the same Phase-1 work pays here.

first_keystroke_after_idle_p50_ms.note: The cold-pipeline tax: single keystrokes after 2 s of quiet — the keystroke users actually feel. Includes drop-recovery: the first present after idle can be dropped; wake-double-present bounds recovery at ~1 tick. Validated 59.5 ms (deadline-driven recovery measured 91.8; broken recovery measured 1735). Improvement path: longer warm window, second immediate present, pipeline-depth work.

first_keystroke_after_idle_max_ms.note: See p50 row. Validated max 62.9 ms. A multi-hundred-ms max means drop recovery is broken.

malloc_bytes_per_keystroke.note: Net malloc bytes per keystroke over the paced window (malloc_zone_statistics delta / n). Design target stays 0 net steady-state; measured ~-22 bytes with direct-to-MTLBuffer instance building. Ratchet the budget down as it proves stable.

L3_transport.note: Loopback numbers are a software floor, not LAN numbers (PLAN.md 3.1). LAN overhead rows gate on the rig against the measured L0 floor.

nagle_spikes_in_10k_msgs.note: Samples >35 ms in an otherwise sub-ms distribution = Nagle/delayed-ACK interaction. noDelay regression detector; BEAM_SABOTAGE_NO_NODELAY=1 proves it can go red.

lan_tcp_echo_overhead_above_floor_p99_ms.method: bench-tcp-echo on rig, minus L0 wired floor

L4_crdt_yrs.note: yrs must reproduce the predecessor's measured Yjs costs (encode 30us/18B, apply 11us) within these budgets before it is committed to.

browse_to_peer_found_ms.note: NWBrowser start -> advertised Bonjour peer in results. Requires Local Network TCC grant; a denial must surface as an explicit error, never a silent miss.

join_to_editing_5mb_workspace_ms.note: Join gesture confirmed -> full snapshot applied and guest can type. Wired.

join_gesture_to_code_visible_ms.note: THE CONNECTION MOMENT. Gesture (click a peer row / press its number) -> the 6-digit verification code is PRESENTED on BOTH screens (max of the two presentedTimes, single machine = one clock domain). This is the number the 'feels instant' claim rests on: everything before a human has to decide anything.

join_confirm_to_editing_ms.note: Host presses return -> guest's editor surface is presented and accepting keystrokes. The half of the join a human is not in.

join_gesture_to_first_shared_keystroke_m.note: HEADLINE, PLAN.md 6 Phase 2 exit: gesture -> ECDH handshake -> code shown+auto-confirmed -> encrypted session -> guest's first keystroke PRESENTED on the host's screen. Auto-confirm means human think time is excluded (deliberately: it is not ours to budget); every millisecond of machine time is included. Discovery time sits in L1.launch_to_peers_visible_ms, so discovery+join < 1 s is these two rows added.

handshake_crypto_cpu_ms.note: X25519 key agreement + HKDF derivation of the two directional session keys and the SAS, measured on the join hot path. Cheap by design; gated so a heavier scheme cannot slip onto the gesture path unnoticed.

L6_end_to_end.note: Wired/Wi-Fi rows need the two-machine rig. The loopback row below is a SOFTWARE FLOOR (PLAN.md 3.1) — it is not a LAN number and never substitutes for one; it exists so a regression in the send/receive/apply/render path is caught on every PR instead of only on the rig.

keystroke_to_remote_present_loopback_p99.note: Guest keystroke t0 -> the frame containing it PRESENTED on the host, both processes on one machine (one mach clock domain, so this is a direct subtraction; the cross-machine rig rows use RTT decomposition instead). Floored by the local present path (60 Hz presented p99 33.8 ms), so this budget is that plus transport+apply headroom — it gates the DELTA, not the frame quantization.

bytes_per_keystroke_on_wire.note: Bytes actually written to the socket per keystroke, ciphertext included (4 B length + AEAD tag + payload). Phase 2 sends a 2-byte op; Phase 3 replaces it with a yrs update and must stay under the same budget.

relay_rtt_under_host_stall_max_ms.note: Guest RTT-probes host relay while host main thread busy-loops 200 ms. Flat only because relay runs on its own thread/event loop — this is that architecture's regression detector (predecessor: <=1.3 ms max).

idle_cpu_connected_pct_core.note: Most collab/Electron apps idle at 3-8%. Deliberate differentiator and battery feature. Measured on loopback from Phase 2: an established encrypted session, both peers quiet, worst of the two processes. This is the gate that makes 'live RTT in the UI' honest — a per-second repaint to animate a number would show up here, which is exactly why the roster repaints only when a displayed value actually changes and why nothing in Beam blinks.

idle_cpu_foreground_alone_pct_core.note: Foreground, no session, no input: event-driven rendering with the display link paused must idle at ~0. BEAM_SABOTAGE_IDLE_SPIN=1 proves the gate can go red.

packaged_launch_ok.note: scripts/verify_app.sh executes the packaged binary DIRECTLY and requires the BEAM_LAUNCH_OK sentinel on stderr + exit 0. The predecessor shipped a silently-broken .app for weeks; this is the never-again gate.
